review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

11:1.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγγίζουσιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ
11:1.targetText: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples

groups.note: ἐγγίζουσιν εἰς "draw near to" is rendered by the transitive verb approached.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a second verb for the second εἰς phrase; the Greek has the one verb ἐγγίζουσιν.
English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.

11:2.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ εὐθὺς εἰσπορευόμενοι εἰς αὐτὴν εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον ἐφ’ ὃν οὐδεὶς οὔπω ἀνθρώπων ἐκάθισεν· λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ φέρετε.
11:2.targetText: and said to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.

groups.note: εἰσπορευόμενοι εἰς "entering into" is rendered as a temporal clause with the transitive verb enter.
With οὐδείς, οὔπω "not yet" is rendered ever.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the partitive ἀνθρώπων (of men) unexpressed; no one covers it.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a location to tied; the Greek has only the participle.
English supplies an object; φέρετε has none in Greek.
English adds a destination; the Greek has only φέρετε (bring).

11:3.sourceText: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ Τί ποιεῖτε τοῦτο; εἴπατε Ὁ Κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει, καὶ εὐθὺς αὐτὸν ἀποστέλλει πάλιν ὧδε.
11:3.targetText: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you doing this?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it and will return it shortly.’”

groups.note: χρείαν ἔχει "has need" is rendered needs.
ἀποστέλλει πάλιν "sends back" is rendered will return.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render ὑμῖν (to you) after asks.
BSB leaves ὧδε (here) implicit in return.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the addressee of tell; the Greek has none.

11:4.sourceText: καὶ ἀπῆλθον καὶ εὗρον πῶλον δεδεμένον πρὸς θύραν ἔξω ἐπὶ τοῦ ἀμφόδου, καὶ λύουσιν αὐτόν.
11:4.targetText: So they went and found the colt outside in the street, tied at a doorway. They untied it,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

11:5.sourceText: καί τινες τῶν ἐκεῖ ἑστηκότων ἔλεγον αὐτοῖς Τί ποιεῖτε λύοντες τὸν πῶλον;
11:5.targetText: and some who were standing there asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”

groups.note: The article with the participle ἑστηκότων is rendered as a relative clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render αὐτοῖς (to them) after asked.

11:6.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ ἀφῆκαν αὐτούς.
11:6.targetText: The disciples answered as Jesus had instructed them, and the people gave them permission.

groups.note: οἱ δέ "and they" is the subject, which BSB names as the disciples.
ἀφῆκαν "they let [them go]" is rendered gave ... permission.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB does not render αὐτοῖς (to them) after answered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; εἶπεν has none in Greek.
English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.

11:7.sourceText: καὶ φέρουσιν τὸν πῶλον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐπιβάλλουσιν αὐτῷ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπ’ αὐτόν.
11:7.targetText: Then they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and He sat on it.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:8.sourceText: καὶ πολλοὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἔστρωσαν εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, ἄλλοι δὲ στιβάδας, κόψαντες ἐκ τῶν ἀγρῶν.
11:8.targetText: Many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the group; the Greek has only πολλοί (many).
English repeats the verb; the Greek leaves ἔστρωσαν understood with ἄλλοι.

11:9.sourceText: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον Ὡσαννά· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου·
11:9.targetText: The ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting:  “Hosanna!”   “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”

groups.note: The article with the participle προάγοντες is rendered as a relative clause.
The article with the participle ἀκολουθοῦντες is rendered those who followed.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has the participle εὐλογημένος alone.

11:10.sourceText: Εὐλογημένη ἡ ἐρχομένη βασιλεία τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Δαυείδ· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.
11:10.targetText: “Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!”   “Hosanna in the highest!”

groups.note: The genitive article τοῦ marks the of-phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has the participle εὐλογημένη alone.

11:11.sourceText: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς τὸ ἱερόν· καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντα, ὀψὲ ἤδη οὔσης τῆς ὥρας, ἐξῆλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.
11:11.targetText: Then Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple courts. He looked around at everything, but since it was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve.

groups.note: εἰσῆλθεν εἰς "went into" is rendered by the transitive verb entered.
The genitive absolute participle οὔσης is rendered as a since-clause.
ὥρας "the hour" is rendered by the impersonal it.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.
English supplies a second verb for the second εἰς phrase; the Greek has the one verb εἰσῆλθεν.
English contrast between the participle clause and the main verb; the Greek has no conjunction here.

11:12.sourceText: Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐπείνασεν.
11:12.targetText: The next day, when they had left Bethany, Jesus was hungry.

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἐξελθόντων ... ἀπό "having gone out from" is rendered when ... had left.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.

11:13.sourceText: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔχουσαν φύλλα ἦλθεν εἰ ἄρα τι εὑρήσει ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐπ’ αὐτὴν οὐδὲν εὗρεν εἰ μὴ φύλλα· ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς οὐκ ἦν σύκων.
11:13.targetText: Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, He went to see if there was any fruit on it. But when He reached it, He found nothing on it except leaves, since it was not the season for figs.

groups.note: εὑρήσει "he would find" is recast as there was.
ἐλθὼν ἐπ’ "coming to" is rendered when ... reached.
εἰ μή together mean except.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB leaves the particle ἄρα (perhaps) unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb to introduce the indirect question εἰ ... εὑρήσει.
English specifies what τι (anything) refers to.
English repeats the location; the Greek has none with οὐδὲν εὗρεν.

11:14.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῇ Μηκέτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἐκ σοῦ μηδεὶς καρπὸν φάγοι. καὶ ἤκουον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
11:14.targetText: Then He said to the tree, “May no one ever eat of your fruit again.” And His disciples heard this statement.

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν "answering said" is rendered said.
The pronoun αὐτῇ (to it) is rendered by the noun.
Μηκέτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα "no longer forever" is rendered ever ... again, with the negation carried by no one.
The optative φάγοι is rendered May ... eat.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; ἤκουον has none in Greek.

11:15.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ τοὺς ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστερὰς κατέστρεψεν,
11:15.targetText: When they arrived in Jerusalem, Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.

groups.note: BSB subordinates the first clause; the καί joining the two clauses is rendered When.
εἰσελθὼν εἰς "going into" is rendered by the transitive verb entered.
The article τούς with πωλοῦντας shares BSB's those who were; BSB reverses the Greek order "selling and buying".
The article with the participle ἀγοράζοντας is rendered as a relative clause.
ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ "in the temple" is condensed to there.

BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

English coordinator; the participle εἰσελθών is rendered as the finite verb entered.

11:16.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν ἵνα τις διενέγκῃ σκεῦος διὰ τοῦ ἱεροῦ,
11:16.targetText: And He would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts.

11:17.sourceText: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Οὐ γέγραπται ὅτι Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν; ὑμεῖς δὲ πεποιήκατε αὐτὸν σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.
11:17.targetText: Then Jesus began to teach them, and He declared, “Is it not written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”

groups.note: The imperfect ἐδίδασκεν is rendered began to teach.
BSB attaches αὐτοῖς (to them), which goes with ἔλεγεν, to teach.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι introducing the quotation is represented only by the colon.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.

11:18.sourceText: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἐζήτουν πῶς αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν· ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ αὐτόν, πᾶς γὰρ ὁ ὄχλος ἐξεπλήσσετο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.
11:18.targetText: When the chief priests and scribes heard this, they looked for a way to kill Him. For they were afraid of Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching.

groups.note: BSB subordinates the first clause; the καί joining the two clauses is rendered When.

11:19.sourceText: Καὶ ὅταν ὀψὲ ἐγένετο, ἐξεπορεύοντο ἔξω τῆς πόλεως.
11:19.targetText: And when evening came, Jesus and His disciples went out of the city.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the plural verb ending.

11:20.sourceText: Καὶ παραπορευόμενοι πρωῒ εἶδον τὴν συκῆν ἐξηραμμένην ἐκ ῥιζῶν.
11:20.targetText: As they were walking back in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots.

groups.note: The participle παραπορευόμενοι is rendered as an As-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the possessive; the Greek says only "from roots".

11:21.sourceText: καὶ ἀναμνησθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ Ῥαββεί, ἴδε ἡ συκῆ ἣν κατηράσω ἐξήρανται.
11:21.targetText: Peter remembered it and said, “Look, Rabbi! The fig tree You cursed has withered.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render αὐτῷ (to Him) after said.
BSB leaves the relative pronoun ἥν (which) unexpressed: "the fig tree You cursed".

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for remembered; the Greek has none.
English coordinator; the participle ἀναμνησθείς is rendered as the finite verb remembered.

11:22.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἔχετε πίστιν θεοῦ.
11:22.targetText: “Have faith in God,” Jesus said to them.

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς ... λέγει "answering says" is rendered said.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:23.sourceText: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ μὴ διακριθῇ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ πιστεύῃ ὅτι ὃ λαλεῖ γίνεται, ἔσται αὐτῷ.
11:23.targetText: “Truly I tell you that if anyone says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen, it will be done for him.

groups.note: ὃς ἄν "whoever" is rendered if anyone.
The dative τῷ ὄρει "to the mountain" supplies to; this belongs to τούτῳ.
The verb διακριθῇ "doubts" is rendered has ... doubt, with μή as no.
ὃ λαλεῖ "what he says" is condensed to it.
The present γίνεται "happens" is rendered will happen.
ἔσται "it will be" is rendered it will be done.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English counterpart with his heart.

11:24.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πάντα ὅσα προσεύχεσθε καὶ αἰτεῖσθε, πιστεύετε ὅτι ἐλάβετε, καὶ ἔσται ὑμῖν.
11:24.targetText: Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο "because of this" is rendered Therefore.
πάντα ὅσα "all things whatever" is rendered whatever.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB folds προσεύχεσθε καὶ αἰτεῖσθε ("you pray and ask") into ask for in prayer.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; ἐλάβετε has none in Greek.

11:25.sourceText: καὶ ὅταν στήκετε προσευχόμενοι, ἀφίετε εἴ τι ἔχετε κατά τινος, ἵνα καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ἀφῇ ὑμῖν τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
11:25.targetText: And when you stand to pray, if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well.”

11:27.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχονται πάλιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. καὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ περιπατοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἔρχονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι,
11:27.targetText: After their return to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking in the temple courts, and the chief priests, scribes, and elders came up to Him.

groups.note: ἔρχονται πάλιν "they come again" is rendered as the noun phrase their return.
BSB subordinates the first clause; the καί joining the clauses is rendered After.
The pronoun αὐτοῦ is rendered by the name.

The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:28.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς; ἢ τίς σοι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ταῦτα ποιῇς;
11:28.targetText: “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You the authority to do them?”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render αὐτῷ (to Him) after they asked.
BSB leaves ταύτην (this) unexpressed: "the authority".

11:29.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐπερωτήσω ὑμᾶς ἕνα λόγον, καὶ ἀποκρίθητέ μοι, καὶ ἐρῶ ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.
11:29.targetText: “I will ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

groups.note: The imperative ἀποκρίθητε followed by καί and a future works as a condition, rendered if you answer.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB does not render αὐτοῖς (to them) after replied.
The καί that follows the conditional imperative has no English word; BSB uses an if-clause instead.

11:30.sourceText: τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ Ἰωάνου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων; ἀποκρίθητέ μοι.
11:30.targetText: John’s baptism—was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me!”

11:31.sourceText: καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ Διὰ τί οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;
11:31.targetText: They deliberated among themselves what they should answer: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

groups.note: Διὰ τί "on account of what" is rendered Why.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The participle λέγοντες (saying) is represented only by the colon before the quotation.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with τί εἴπωμεν ("what should we say"), which N1904 lacks.

11:32.sourceText: ἀλλὰ εἴπωμεν Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;— ἐφοβοῦντο τὸν ὄχλον· ἅπαντες γὰρ εἶχον τὸν Ἰωάνην ὄντως ὅτι προφήτης ἦν.
11:32.targetText: But if we say, ‘From men’...” they were afraid of the people, for they all held that John truly was a prophet.

groups.note: The deliberative subjunctive εἴπωμεν "should we say" is rendered as a condition.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:33.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγουσιν Οὐκ οἴδαμεν. καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.
